context:
Follow the pattern in benchbox/core/visualization/ascii/diverging_bar.py for the
centered-zero layout with bars extending left and right from a reference line:

1. Create SpeedupData dataclass (name, ratio, is_baseline).
2. Create ASCIINormalizedSpeedup(ASCIIChartBase) with a render() method.
3. Draw a vertical baseline reference line at 1.0x in the center.
4. Ratios > 1.0 extend right (faster, green), ratios < 1.0 extend left (slower, red).
5. Add from_normalized_results() factory that computes ratios given results + baseline name.
6. Use logarithmic scaling for the bar width to handle large ratio ranges (e.g., 0.1x to 50x).

The baseline platform selection should accept either a platform name or "slowest"/"fastest"
as convenience aliases.
description:
Add a new ASCII chart type that shows platform performance as a ratio relative to a
user-selected baseline platform (e.g., "DuckDB is 3.2x faster than SQLite"). The
baseline is rendered at 1.0x with a vertical reference line. Platforms faster than
baseline extend right, slower ones extend left.

This is the standard way TPC and SPEC results are formally reported. When comparing
platforms that span orders of magnitude (50ms to 50,000ms), absolute bar charts make
fast platforms invisible slivers. Normalized ratios make relative performance
immediately clear regardless of absolute magnitude.

Example output:
```
Normalized Performance (baseline: SQLite = 1.0x)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
         Slower          │         Faster
SQLite                   │█  1.0x
Pandas             ██████│   0.4x
DuckDB                   │████████████████████  8.2x
Polars                   │██████████████████  7.5x
ClickHouse               │██████████████████████████  12.1x
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

This is distinct from the existing bar chart (absolute values) and the diverging bar
chart (percentage change between two runs of the same platform). The normalized speedup
chart shows cross-platform comparison ratios with a centered baseline reference.

anti_patterns.why: they serve different purposes (absolute values, pct change)

anti_patterns.dont: use linear scaling for bar widths
anti_patterns.instead: use log2 scaling so 2x and 0.5x are symmetric around the baseline

preserves.behavior: ASCIIBarChart behavior unchanged (this is a new chart type, not a modification)
All 9 existing chart types continue to render identically
render_ascii_chart() in exporters.py handles all existing chart_type strings

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "from benchbox.core.visualization.ascii.normalized_speedup import ASCIINormalizedSpeedup, SpeedupData; data = [SpeedupData('SQLite', 1.0, True), SpeedupData('DuckDB', 8.2, False), SpeedupData('Pandas', 0.4, False)]; chart = ASCIINormalizedSpeedup(data=data); print(chart.render())"
verifications.description: New chart class renders without error
verifications.expected: Rendered chart with baseline at center and bars extending left/right
